title: Yankees’ Giancarlo Stanton’s return is now further in doubt as slugger faces setback
content:
TORONTO — The bad injury news has continued for the New York Yankees.

Giancarlo Stanton sustained a setback during his return from a strained right calf that has sidelined him since April 24, Yankees manager Aaron Boone said Saturday afternoon.

The setback occurred as Stanton was running the bases in recent days, when he tweaked his right calf. Boone noted that further imaging might be necessary to determine if the slugger needs to decelerate his current progression. While the Yankees previously anticipated that Stanton could be back in the lineup for the start of the upcoming homestand against the Chicago White Sox on Tuesday, that timeline is now uncertain.

“That’s kind of slowed him down — not slowed him down — I expected him back early in this homestand, but that’s in jeopardy now,” Boone said.

Before this latest hurdle, Stanton appeared to be on the verge of a return, having started live batting practice sessions at Yankee Stadium over the past week. Because he’s a designated hitter, the veteran slugger has tended to bypass a traditional minor-league rehab assignment. Instead, he typically prepares by facing live arms and logging at-bats against the Trajekt, an advanced pitching machine designed to replicate the specific deliveries of big-league pitchers.

When Stanton initially injured his calf, the Yankees believed that the 36-year-old would not have to miss much time. His absence is now approaching two months, and it’s unclear when he’ll be able to return.

Without Stanton and Aaron Judge, who’s sidelined with a stress fracture in his rib, the Yankees don’t have either of their best right-handed hitters. That has made them susceptible to being attacked by left-handed relievers. As an example of how left-handed New York’s lineup has become in Stanton’s and Judge’s absences, the Yankees have a lane of five consecutive lefties in their lineup against the Toronto Blue Jays on Saturday.

Before Saturday’s game, the Yankees also placed center fielder Trent Grisham on the injured list with a strained right hamstring. The Yankees do not know the severity of Grisham’s strain, as he’s scheduled to undergo imaging when the club is back in New York on Monday. The Yankees started Cody Bellinger in left field, Spencer Jones in center field and Jasson Domínguez in right field in their first game without Grisham. Saturday’s game is also the first of Domínguez’s career that he’ll play right field in the majors.

“The way I have the alignment could evolve here over the next several days, but by all accounts, the last few days have gone really well, and how he’s taken to it, so I just feel like I want to give it a look,” Boone said. “Hopefully this alignment is something that can work for us here in the near-term, but it’s something I’ll be paying attention to, and it doesn’t mean I won’t flip some things as we go.”

Domínguez was initially viewed as Stanton’s replacement at DH back in April, but with Judge and Grisham now sidelined, the 23-year-old will now have the opportunity for an extended run at a new position.
